applied.summary: Committee (audio, web-verified): original claimed undithered truncation causes "sudden full-scale artifacts that risk hearing and speaker damage" — inaccurate. Undithered truncation produces signal-correlated (harmonic) quantization distortion, not full-scale/safety artifacts. Rewritten to the correct effect; removed the erroneous UNSAFE hazard claim. Confirmed vs quantization/dither literature (Quantization and Dither: A Theoretical Survey; AllAboutCircuits dithering articles).

Committee (audio, web-verified): original conflated sitar and sarod plectra. Corrected: sitar uses the wire mizrab worn on the finger; the sarod is played with a hand-held java (jawa) plectrum. Confirmed vs India Instruments encyclopedia, Chandraveena, and sarod pedagogy sources. plain_english FK=6.1.

declined.reason: DECLINED — two committee experts assumed "RipX DeepMix" is a real Hit'n'Mix product and asked to author the full entry. Web-verified against the manufacturer (hitnmix.com) and Sound on Sound / MusicTech reviews: RipX editions are DeepAudio, DeepRemix, DeepCreate (+ RipX DAW / DAW PRO). No "DeepMix" exists. Authoring it would require inventing a nonexistent product, violating FLAG-DON'T-GUESS. Entry remains FLAG-FOR-REVIEW for Booth to confirm the intended term (likely RipX DeepRemix or RipX DAW).
